# lighthouse-ab

Use this skill when a change is supposed to make a page faster and the claim has to survive a second run. It ships `scripts/lh-ab.mjs`, a dependency-free runner that enforces the measurement protocol so no step can be skipped; the skill is the protocol around it.

## Triggers

- "did this make the page faster", "measure the perf impact", "A/B these two builds"
- A PR description about to state a Lighthouse score, LCP, TBT or CLS number
- Two deployments or two local builds of the same page to compare
- A page that needs a baseline series before any work starts (`--a` only)

## Protocol

### Step 1 — Decide what is being compared

```text
Same page, two versions?
  Two deployed URLs (preview vs production, before vs after a deploy)
    → pass both; same tier, same CDN state, same consent-banner state
  Two local builds
    → a production build of each (`next build && next start`, `astro build && astro preview`, `vite preview`, …)
      on two ports, against the same database and content
    → an HTTP/2 proxy in front when the score matters: Lighthouse's simulator models plain HTTP
      and HTTP/3 as HTTP/1.1 and scores them 8–10 points lower
  Local vs deployed
    → not comparable (runner CPU, latency, CDN). Local with local, deployed with deployed
One page, nothing to compare?
  → `--a` only: a baseline series with the same controls
```

Each variant MUST render a distinguishing string — a build id or commit sha in a meta tag, a `?dpl=` suffix on an asset. Pass it as `--marker-a` / `--marker-b`: a run whose served HTML lacks its marker is discarded, which is what catches "the previous build answered" after a server switch.

### Step 2 — Run

```bash
node .claude/skills/lighthouse-ab/scripts/lh-ab.mjs \
  --a=http://localhost:3000/page --label-a=base   --marker-a=abc1234 \
  --b=http://localhost:3001/page --label-b=change --marker-b=def5678 \
  --runs=5 --block=consent.example.com,googletagmanager.com --out=lh-ab
```

The runner needs Node 20+ and a Chrome; it fetches a pinned Lighthouse with `npx` unless `LIGHTHOUSE_BIN` points at one. What it does, and why none of it is optional:

- One Chrome with `--disable-quic` and a fresh profile; one discarded warm-up per variant (a cold GPU and code cache cost 2–3 s on the first frame and read as a low score with nothing wrong)
- A and B interleaved, the order swapped every round, so neither variant gets the warmer machine
- Storage reset left on — `--disable-storage-reset` keeps the HTTP cache and silently switches throttling to devtools
- A run discarded when the document was not a 2xx from the measured origin or a first-party script, stylesheet or font failed: a login or gate page scores 60–80 on a tiny document
- Protocol mix and per-origin server latency logged per run, because both move scores with no code change
- `summary.md` (pasteable) and `summary.json`; `--html` keeps the HTML reports

Flags worth knowing: `--preset=desktop`; `--cpu=N` sets the simulated CPU multiplier (4 is Lighthouse's mobile default and what PageSpeed Insights uses; on a fast laptop 6 approximates a 2-vCPU CI runner's TBT, 20 overshoots); `--long` adds a 6 s window after `load`, which is what PageSpeed Insights records and the default trace window does not; `--block=` removes third parties whose state varies per run; `--runs=` is 5 at minimum and 12 or more for a delta inside ±5.

Never pass an auth token through `--extra-headers` to reach a gated host: Lighthouse writes every value into every report, JSON and HTML. Use a bypass the host accepts, or inject the header through the DevTools protocol on the page's own origin.

### Step 3 — Read the verdict

The runner prints one, but judge it yourself:

```text
Every change run above every base run (or every one below)?
  YES → real; report it
  NO  → is the median delta larger than the spread (max − min) of either variant?
          YES → likely real; raise runs to ≥12 before claiming it
          NO  → not shown. Combine with other levers and measure the set, or drop it
                (three changes inside the noise alone measured +3.5 together)
Different LCP element between A and B?
  → the change altered WHAT is measured, not how fast it is; say so, the scores are not comparable
Runs split into two clusters on FCP?
  → bimodal; compare within a cluster and judge by the lower one
```

### Step 4 — Report

```text
BAD:  "Lighthouse went from 85 to 91."
      (two runs, cache state unknown, runner and Lighthouse version unstated)

GOOD: | variant | runs | performance (runs) | min / med / max | LCP med | TBT med | before LCP med |
      | base    | 5    | 83, 85, 84, 86, 85 | 83 / 85 / 86    | 3.9 s   | 410 ms  | 318 kB         |
      | change  | 5    | 90, 91, 89, 91, 92 | 89 / 91 / 92    | 3.2 s   | 380 ms  | 241 kB         |
      Lighthouse 13.4.1 · mobile · cpu ×4 · QUIC off · blocked: consent, GTM · local h2 proxy
      Every change run above every base run (median +6).
```

Local numbers are local. Never put them in a column next to CI or PageSpeed Insights numbers, and never draw one trend line across two runners, tiers or Lighthouse versions.

## Completion checklist

- [ ] Both variants served the same way: production builds, same tier, same content
- [ ] Markers passed, and no run discarded for a missing marker — or each discard explained
- [ ] At least 5 counted runs per variant, interleaved; 12 or more when the delta is inside ±5
- [ ] LCP element identical across variants, or the difference called out
- [ ] The report carries the run list, min and median, Lighthouse version, preset, CPU multiplier and blocked patterns

## When NOT to use

- The question is about real users: use field data (CrUX, Search Console), not a lab run
- Load or concurrency: use the `k6-load-testing` skill
- The cause of a low score is unknown: attribute first with `perf-attribution`, then A/B the fix
